patch_description:
Building on the strongest prior candidate (global RY + global RZ single-qubit layer, followed by a shared-angle CRZ entangler applied across multiple ring "shells", tied across all 3 repeated blocks), two key empirical lessons are combined into a new, more parameter-frugal design:

1. The ablation that diversified entangler axes per shell (CRX/CRY/CRZ) scored *worse* than keeping a single CRZ axis everywhere, so axis-uniformity is preserved and even reinforced (all entangling gates stay CRZ).
2. The evolution guidance states parameter count reduction always improves score, with no diminishing returns, so the two single-qubit rotation angles ("theta_ry", "theta_rz") are merged into ONE shared parameter "theta1" reused by both the RY and RZ gates on every qubit -- this halves the single-qubit-layer parameter count while still producing a genuine (non-trivial) fixed-axis single-qubit rotation direction (RZ(theta1)*RY(theta1)), which becomes richer once composed across the 3 tied repetitions and combined with entangling.

To compensate for the reduced single-qubit flexibility, the entangling structure is completed into FULL ring connectivity: distances 1, 2, 3, and 4 on the 8-qubit ring together cover every one of the 28 possible qubit pairs exactly once, all still driven by a single shared angle "theta_ent" via CRZ. This gives the circuit maximal correlation-building power between any two qubits (hence any dataset-chosen unknown readout pair) while using only 2 distinct circuit parameters (4 total with gain/bias) -- fewer than every previously tried candidate, aiming to score higher on the parameter-economy term while preserving or improving robust worst-group margin through denser entanglement.
